I like this game! It's pretty fun, movement is pretty smooth and shooting's alright, I like the lo-fi graphics, the gameplay is fast and engaging and the setting is pretty funny. My two main negative points though: the purple enemies that shoot guns make maps WAY harder and sometimes feel unfair, and dying; making your upgrades lose two levels is a really odd punishiment mechanic that just isn't much fun... Risking playing and losing all your progress from a randomly way more difficult encounter doesn't make me want to restart -- it just leaves me frustrated and makes me want to rage quit. Quick edit: there's also a pretty annoying bug where if you pause the game while there is a pop up message in the game, your mouse becomse unlocked from the game screen, making you click and open stuff on your desktop while you're playing.

More than worth the money! Great little game, that has a ton of potential for additions and growth. Very smooth experience with only a couple complaints about that game. If you're wondering whether or not spending the 5.00 to try it. Just do it. Totally worth it. The gameplay, atmosphere, and concept is solid. There are some minor bugs, where a menu will stay open and won't go away, forcing you to restart (rare). I wish the "chat" in game was using an LLM of some sort, cause it would create a great opportunity where you want to perform well, but chat could be distracting cause you're wondering what "chat" is saying. But as of right now, it will get to a point where the chats are the same and redundant. I wont complain about that too much though, cause I'm not a dev, and I have no idea how hard that would be to implement. My one glaring criticism though is the snipers...... It totally ruins the enjoyment of what makes this game fun sometimes. The way that the combo/kill system works is that it resets if you take any damage. The snipers will ruin this for you to the point where you almost dont care to keep the combo going, and getting is as high as possible. you could have a 50 to 100 killstreak combo going, just for a sniper shot to come flying out of the crowd and rob you of it. Which normally be fine, but the snipers are wierd in this game. No visual indicator (like a sniper line idk what they are called), they shoot fast, their hit box is tiny, and when you're starting out, they're pretty dang tanky. So early game before upgrades, they can just ruin your run. So I would suggest playing with how they work (not removing them). I would say rework the combo system, BUT it actually feels really REALLY good to hold a combo knowing that you're a GAMER and not getting hit. One more small complaint is the quest system. There should be some kind of weighting so that you always get at least 1 quest that you can do. Sometimes 3 quests will pop up that you can't even work towards, and have to wait until the next rest room, so idk. Also if you read this far, I beat the game NEVER taking the shield, so now you have to as well. (Dev just remove the shield upgrade from the game >:) ) Just to emphasize again, BUY THIS GAME! IT'S GOING PLACES!)

Are there a couple of issues i have with the "donation system" I have? yeah but I also have only been playing 5 hours, and thats not near enough time where i consider myself an expert on a game like this so its possibly just a skill issue Excited to see where the game heads to and Im pretty happy to recommend this to anyone looking for a fast boomer shooter like experience in a roguelike/lite package.

Luckrot is a game set in a dystopian future where Elon Musk was successful in his attempt to become the shadow president of the United States and kick is bigger than amazon. I think everyone can agree that the appeal of a “boomer shooter” is the high octane gameplay, that's the thing that these games consistently have over AAA shooters, as the latter tends to put more effort into graphical fidelity or showmanship than gameplay, and this is true for luckrot but it doesn't mean that it has lackluster presentation. The brutalist look of the arenas, the design of the freaks, etc, the game has a lot of things that aids in its presentation and world building; my favorite of these is how the un-upgraded weapons look uninteresting and the upgrades are just, vials of green goo, as if, the only weapons that the streamer can get are bargain bin used guns. Speaking of guns they are pretty basic, you have your ARs, your shotguns, your sniper rifles, etc. However this is not a detriment in my opinion, as I’ve mentioned before, the lack of futuristic guns helps with worldbuilding but it also means that the learning curve is non-existent, you can immediately hop on the game and understand what each gun does. Movement also doesn't get too crazy; you have your double jump, slide, dodge, as well as wall jumping, nothing out of the ordinary but I must remark that the movement in this game is very responsive. One of my criticisms of the game is adjacent to this, the movement is indeed responsive and fun, and so, this game is at its best when you're hopping around shooting enemies while wall jumping and such, however, weapons like the AR and specially the burst riffle work best while stationary so I never really go for those weapons and getting then on the lootbox feels wasteful. One of the most unique aspects of this game is the progression, Weapons and buddy bots are upgraded by gambling your donations (after their cut) for the little vials of green goo, and if you die in the middle of a run you don't lose all your upgrades just 1 level, so if your shotgun is level three when you die, the next time you play and you roll a shotgun it will be level 2. I like this, in rogue-likes every run is imminently consequential, as you gain experience and learn the game a little bit more, but in this game doomed runs are materially consequential as well, it makes it so runs that you're clearly going to lose feel not so senseless. Besides guns you also get upgrades for your playable character, another criticism I have is that these feel particularly unbalanced, some are very strong, like higher rate of fire and the double wield, and some are very weak like the grapple or the death penalty. I love the freaks, all of their designs feel iconic to me, they look silly while in constant pain, they also make very compelling enemies, with a mixture of clever AI and good spawning points it makes it almost impossible to funnel them into a corridor and shoot them until they all die, this is because if you remain stationary for a while it won't be long until some of the freaks try to flank you, the magenta freaks stay behind the other freaks or far away from you so they can snipe you, the blue freaks slow you down making it easier for the other freaks to hit you, etc; and while, for the most part, the freaks per room number, is very manageable in act 1, act 2 and 3 they become actual swarms, and letting then backing you into a corner can lead to you losing most of your health if not to the end of your run. I love the balancing of the freaks in act 2 and 3, but if I had any criticisms here it would be that I think health drops are a bit scarce, as I've said, in those rooms the number of freaks gets crazy, and so, you need to play it safe, shoot a little into to hoard and back up to regen some of your health and do it again, I think that if health were to drop more often it could give the player a bit more confidence in playing riskier; or maybe this is a skill issue on my part. In conclusion: I love this game and I highly recommend it. One of my favorites of the year so far.

I have been loving the art style, guns and gambling my money away for upgrades but theres alot that just falls short in the game for me. I like how it is a live stream and people chat and send money but the messages get annoying. The bosses die in 10 seconds. there is no point at all to melee because you will get hit by the enemy instantly. The areas to fight in get repetitive and I find myself just grouping up enemies to die to explosive barrels to kill alot of them which is okay but defeats the purpose of running and gunning. I could have a 70 killstreak and the game still throws out text saying BORING. Not sure why the other negative review says the shotgun is bad when I think its the most op and having the double gun ability makes me mow through the bosses. for $5 its not a terrible game but its not that great either. Just needs to get some things fixed. Also been having issues whenever I get an upgrade my curser will just disappear and I have to tab out of the game and go back in for it to appear and chose an upgrade

feels a little like a Serious Sam game, but braindead. no actual need for dancing with weapons, you just run around the map spamming or holding LMB. it gets old really quick, all of the arenas feel the same, there are just more enemies as the game goes on. and even the bosses are all really the same, and theyre easier than the actual waves of enemies, just because its holding LMB over one target instead of aiming at others too. all of them are badly designed the only positive thing about this game is the artstyle - i like the idea behind it, but still, its actual execution is of amateur quality. and despite the graphics trying to look like a 2000s game, it can get really laggy in the later stages, just bad optimization. dont recommend, its fun for the first 15 minutes and tolerable for the next 45, beyond the first hour i dont see why anyone would play this, its bad, but theres a good core idea the dev or devs can work on i guess
